Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 27, verses 1–3:

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-Naml (The Ant)

Al-Mahayimi said: It is named after it (the ant), because it includes its saying, which indicates the knowledge of animals of the innocence of the prophets and their followers from deliberately committing what is disliked, and this is among the things that necessitate trust in them. And this is among the greatest aims of the Qur'an. It is a Meccan surah, and its verses are ninety-three.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Discussion on the interpretation of His, the Exalted, saying:

﴿Ta-Sin. These are the verses of the Qur'an and a clear Book.﴾ ﴿A guidance and good tidings for the believers,﴾ ﴿who establish prayer, give zakah, and are certain of the Hereafter.﴾

﴿Ta-Sin. These are the verses of the Qur'an and a clear Book.﴾ The reference is to the surah itself. "The Qur'an" denotes the whole, or the entirety of what was revealed. That is: this surah is among the verses of the Qur'an, which is known for its exalted status, and verses of a Book of great magnitude, clarifying what it contains of judgments, rulings, admonitions and lessons. ﴿A guidance and good tidings for the believers,﴾ ﴿who establish prayer, give zakah, and are certain of the Hereafter.﴾ That is: it is a guidance from misguidance, and good tidings of Allah's mercy and good pleasure, for those who believe and do righteous deeds, such as establishing prayer and giving zakah, and who are certain of the Hereafter and of the recompense for deeds, good and bad.

A subtle point:

The repetition of the pronoun (in "wa-hum", "hum") is for the purpose of restriction and specification, according to what is in al-Kashshaf (al-Kashshaf, Zamakhshari's exegesis).

The author of al-Intisaf (Ibn al-Munir) has another view. He said: Since the original sentence was "and they are certain of the Hereafter," and then he placed the prepositional phrase before its governing verb, for the sake of emphasis on it, so it came to separate the subject from the predicate. It was therefore desired that the predicate follow the subject directly, and the prepositional phrase had come between them, so he repeated mention of it so that the predicate would follow. The intended emphasis on the prepositional phrase was not lost, since it remained in its place, fronted. It is not objectionable that the word be repeated separately after what requires the repetition. The closest parallel to this is the poet's saying:

Ask Dhu [...] and hasten Dha, and join us to Dha al-shahm (fat), for we have grown weary of it with vinegar.

(p-4657) The original would be "and join us to dha al-shahm," so it fell at the middle or end of the line (according to the view that a half-line of rajaz is a complete verse) at the lam. The poet built on the premise that at the middle or end there must be some pause. So by that pause he allowed a distance between the defined noun and the article of definition, and repeated it a second time. This repetition did not depend on there being between the first and the repeated word anything, not even one word, other than his supposed slight pause alone.

Then he said: Reflect on this section, for it is worthy of reflection. And Allah knows best.

Then the conditions of the believers are contrasted with the conditions of the disbelievers, in His, the Exalted, saying:

Then the conditions of the believers are contrasted with the conditions of the disbelievers, in His, the Exalted, saying:

The discussion of the words of the Exalted: "Indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter – We have made attractive to them their deeds, so they wander blindly." (27:4) That is, We extended them in their deviation, so they wander in their misguidance. This was a recompense for their denial of the Final Abode and of the recompense for deeds, as the Exalted said: "And We turn their hearts and their sight away, as they did not believe in it the first time." (6:110)

"Those are the ones for whom is the worst of punishment, and in the Hereafter they are the greatest losers." (27:5) That is, the most severe of people in loss of salvation and of Allah's reward.

"And indeed, you are receiving the Qur'an from the presence of One Wise, Knowing." (27:6) That is, you are being given it and taught it from the side of One Wise in His command and prohibition, Knowing of affairs both apparent and hidden. So His report is pure truth and far-reaching wisdom, as He said: "And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice." (6:115) The sentence is resumptive, brought after the explanation of some of the matters of the Noble Qur'an, as a preparation for what follows of the magnificent reports. He began with what occurred concerning Musa, peace be upon him, his being chosen and his being given the clear signs, which humbled his opponents and made them an example of evil.

So He, glorified is He, said: "When Musa said to his family..." (27:7) That is, when he turned back from Madyan toward Egypt and lost the way: "Indeed, I have perceived a fire" – that is, I saw it; "I will bring you from it some information" – that is, about the way; "or bring you a burning brand so that you may warm yourselves" – that is, a kindled flame; "so that you may warm yourselves by it." (27:7) "So when he came to it, he was called: 'Blessed is whoever is in the fire and whoever is around it.'" (27:8) That is, blessed is whoever is in the place of the fire and whoever is around its place. Its place is the spot in which it occurred. This is indicated by the reading of Ubayy: "Blessed is the land and whoever is around it," and by a narration from him: "The fire has been blessed." What the spot was blessed for, and those in it and around it were blessed for, is the occurrence of a religious matter there, namely Allah's speaking to Musa, His making him a prophet, and the manifestation of miracles through him. Often a good thing renews itself in some of the regions, and Allah spreads the blessing of that good into its farthest parts and disseminates the traces of its benefit into its remote areas. So how about such a magnificent matter that took place in that blessed spot? Thus in (al-Kashshaf).

Al-Samin said: "Baraka" is transitive by itself, which is why it is constructed in the passive: "Barakaka Allah" (may Allah bless you), "baraka 'alayka," "baraka fika," and "baraka laka." The intended sense of "man" (whoever) is either the Creator, the Exalted, and this is with an elided noun, meaning: from His power and authority in the fire. It was also said that what is meant is Musa and the angels. Likewise His saying "and whoever is around it." It was also said that what is meant by "man" is non-rational beings, namely the light and the places around it. End.

Therefore al-Zamakhshari said: "The apparent meaning is that it is general for everyone who was in that land and in that valley and around them both from the land of Sham." He said: "Allah has marked the land of Sham with blessings in His saying: 'And We delivered him and Lut to the land which We had blessed for the worlds.' (21:71) It was fitting that it be so. It is the place where the prophets, peace and blessings of Allah be upon them, were sent, the descent place of revelation to them, and their gathering place, alive and dead."

Then he said: "The meaning of Allah beginning His address to Musa with this when he came is that it is good news for him that a great matter has passed, from which blessing spreads throughout the entire land of Sham." End.

Al-Qurtubi said: "This is a greeting from Allah, the Exalted, to Musa, and an honouring of him, just as He greeted Ibrahim through the tongues of the angels when they entered upon him and said: 'The mercy of Allah and His blessings be upon you, O people of the house.'"

From Ibn Abbas: "That fire was not fire; it was only a light that blazed." And from him: "It is the light of the Lord of the worlds."

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Abu Ubayda, from Abu Musa, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed Allah does not sleep, nor is it fitting for Him to sleep. He lowers the scale and raises it. The deed of the night is raised to Him before the deed of the day, and the deed of the day before the night. His veil is light, or fire. Were He to uncover it, the splendours of His face would burn everything that His sight reaches." Then Abu Ubayda recited: "That blessed is whoever is in the fire and whoever is around it." (27:8)

Ibn Kathir said: The root of this hadith is recorded in Sahih Muslim from the hadith of Amr ibn Murrah.

"And glorified is Allah, Lord of the worlds." (27:8) That is, the One who does what He wills, none of His creatures resembles Him, none of His creations encompasses Him, and He is the Most High, the Mighty, distinct from all created things; neither the earth nor the heavens contain Him. Rather He is the One, the Self-Sufficient, far exalted above resemblance to originated things. Thus said Ibn Kathir.

He indicated that the context required transcendence, to repel the suggestion of what is unfitting of likeness. Then Musa, peace be upon him, was informed by the Exalted that it is He who speaks to him and communes with him, not an angel nor any other creature, but His exalted Essence, which deserves divinity and the sacred attributes. Then he said: "The meaning of Allah beginning His address to Musa with this when he came is that it is good news for him that a great matter has passed, from which blessing spreads throughout the entire land of Sham." End.

Al-Qurtubi said: "This is a greeting from Allah, the Exalted, to Musa, and an honouring of him, just as He greeted Ibrahim through the tongues of the angels when they entered upon him and said: 'The mercy of Allah and His blessings be upon you, O people of the house.'"

From Ibn Abbas: "That fire was not fire; it was only a light that blazed." And from him: "It is the light of the Lord of the worlds."

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Abu Ubayda, from Abu Musa, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed Allah does not sleep, nor is it fitting for Him to sleep. He lowers the scale and raises it. The deed of the night is raised to Him before the deed of the day, and the deed of the day before the night. His veil is light, or fire. Were He to uncover it, the splendours of His face would burn everything that His sight reaches." Then Abu Ubayda recited: "That blessed is whoever is in the fire and whoever is around it." (27:8)

Ibn Kathir said: The root of this hadith is recorded in Sahih Muslim from the hadith of Amr ibn Murrah.

"And glorified is Allah, Lord of the worlds." (27:8) That is, the One who does what He wills, none of His creatures resembles Him, none of His creations encompasses Him, and He is the Most High, the Mighty, distinct from all created things; neither the earth nor the heavens contain Him. Rather He is the One, the Self-Sufficient, far exalted above resemblance to originated things. Thus said Ibn Kathir.

He indicated that the context required transcendence, to repel the suggestion of what is unfitting of likeness. Then Musa, peace be upon him, was informed by the Exalted that it is He who speaks to him and communes with him, not an angel nor any other creature, but His exalted Essence, which deserves divinity and the sacred attributes. So glorified is He said:

The discussion of the words of the Exalted: "Indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter – We have made attractive to them their deeds, so they wander blindly." (27:4) That is, We extended them in their deviation, so they wander in their misguidance. This was a recompense for their denial of the Final Abode and of the recompense for deeds, as the Exalted said: "And We turn their hearts and their sight away, as they did not believe in it the first time." (6:110)

"Those are the ones for whom is the worst of punishment, and in the Hereafter they are the greatest losers." (27:5) That is, the most severe of people in loss of salvation and of Allah's reward.

"And indeed, you are receiving the Qur'an from the presence of One Wise, Knowing." (27:6) That is, you are being given it and taught it from the side of One Wise in His command and prohibition, Knowing of affairs both apparent and hidden. So His report is pure truth and far-reaching wisdom, as He said: "And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice." (6:115) The sentence is resumptive, brought after the explanation of some of the matters of the Noble Qur'an, as a preparation for what follows of the magnificent reports. He began with what occurred concerning Musa, peace be upon him, his being chosen and his being given the clear signs, which humbled his opponents and made them an example of evil.

So He, glorified is He, said: "When Musa said to his family..." (27:7) That is, when he turned back from Madyan toward Egypt and lost the way: "Indeed, I have perceived a fire" – that is, I saw it; "I will bring you from it some information" – that is, about the way; "or bring you a burning brand so that you may warm yourselves" – that is, a kindled flame; "so that you may warm yourselves by it." (27:7) "So when he came to it, he was called: 'Blessed is whoever is in the fire and whoever is around it.'" (27:8) That is, blessed is whoever is in the place of the fire and whoever is around its place. Its place is the spot in which it occurred. So how about such a magnificent matter that took place in that blessed spot? Thus in (al-Kashshaf).

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 27, verse 9–12:

(p-4660) The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[9–12] ﴿O Musa, indeed it is I, Allah, the Almighty, the Wise.﴾ ﴿And throw down your staff.﴾ So when he saw it moving as if it were a snake, he turned back fleeing and did not return. ﴿O Musa, do not fear; indeed, those sent (as messengers) do not fear in My presence.﴾ [an-Naml: 10] ﴿Except one who wrongs, then substitutes good after evil—indeed, I am Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ [an-Naml: 11] ﴿And insert your hand into your pocket; it will come out white without disease, among nine signs to Pharaoh and his people. Indeed, they have been a defiantly disobedient people.﴾ [an-Naml: 12]

﴿O Musa, indeed it is I, Allah, the Almighty, the Wise.﴾ In the choice of these magnificent names there is a wondrous secret, namely the general indication toward the essence of his mission, peace be upon him. That is: I am Allah, not those objects of worship to which the people of Pharaoh devoted themselves; the Almighty, the Victorious, the Subduer of every tyrant and rebel; the Wise in the commissioning and sending, and in bestowing grace and favour. Then Allah, exalted is He, commanded him to throw his staff from his hand, so as to show him a clear proof that He is capable of everything, by His saying: ﴿And throw down your staff. So when he saw it moving as if it were a snake﴾ [an-Naml: 10]. The jann is a kind of serpent, the swiftest in movement and the most agitated: ﴿turned back﴾ [an-Naml: 10], that is, out of fear; ﴿fleeing and did not return﴾ [an-Naml: 10], that is, did not come back on his heels out of the intensity of his fear. ﴿O Musa, do not fear; indeed, those sent do not fear in My presence﴾ [an-Naml: 10], that is, because of My protection of them, My care for them, and My preserving them from what would harm them. In this there is good news to him of his being chosen for messengerhood and prophethood, and encouragement to him by removing fear, since he cannot carry out the mission so long as his fear of the one to whom he is sent has not been removed. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Except one who wrongs, then substitutes good after evil—indeed, I am Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [an-Naml: 11] is a disconnected exception (istithna' munqati'). It was introduced to correct what might occur to the mind of a general negation of fear for all of them, since some of them may have committed a minor lapse of the kind that is permissible for prophets, peace and blessings be upon them. Yet even if something of that sort proceeded from them, they immediately did what nullifies it, and thereby deserve from Allah, exalted is He, forgiveness and mercy. It is said that by this he intended an allusion to what occurred from (p-4661) Musa, peace be upon him, in his striking of the Qibti and his seeking forgiveness. Abu al-Su'ud said this, and al-Zamakhshari preceded him, saying: "It is likely that by this he intends an allusion to what he (Musa) felt toward Musa." It is one of the allusions whose meaning is subtle, and He named it wrongdoing just as Musa said: ﴿My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself, so forgive me﴾ [al-Qasas: 16]. Then Allah, exalted is He, pointed to another miraculous sign besides the staff, which He gave him, by His saying: ﴿And insert your hand into your pocket; it will come out white without disease﴾ [an-Naml: 12], that is, without any affliction such as leprosy: ﴿among nine signs﴾ [an-Naml: 12], that is, other than these, which you will be given when Pharaoh denies your messengerhood. These are: striking the water of the river with the staff so that it turns into blood; the frogs spreading over the land of Egypt; the lice, when he strikes the dust and the land fills with lice; the locusts sent upon them; the severe plague; affliction of their bodies with sores, boils and pustules; the destruction of their harvests by severe hail; and their being covered with thick darkness, as has been narrated. Regarding "nine" there are several readings: the first is that it is a third circumstantial phrase, meaning: a sign goes forth among nine signs. The second is that it is connected to an omitted verb, meaning: go among nine. The third is that it is connected to His saying: ﴿And throw down your staff﴾ [an-Naml: 10] and ﴿insert your hand﴾ [an-Naml: 12], meaning: among the totality of nine signs. And "fi" here has the meaning of "ma'a" (with): ﴿to Pharaoh﴾ [an-Naml: 12], meaning: sent with them to Pharaoh, ﴿and his people. Indeed, they have been a defiantly disobedient people﴾ [an-Naml: 12], meaning: transgressing the limits, in disbelief and aggression. This is a justification for the sending.

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[13–16] ﴿So when Our signs came to them, clearly visible, they said, "This is manifest magic."﴾ ﴿And they denied them, though their souls were convinced of them, out of wrongdoing and arrogance. So see how was the end of the corrupters.﴾ [An-Naml: 14] ﴿And We had certainly given knowledge to Dawud and Sulayman, and they said, "All praise is for Allah, who has favored us over many of His believing servants."﴾ [An-Naml: 15] (p-4662) ﴿And Sulayman inherited from Dawud and said, "O people, we have been taught the speech of birds, and we have been given of all things. **On the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:**

[17–25] ﴿And for Solomon were gathered his soldiers of the jinn and mankind and the birds, and they were marshaled in ranks.﴾ ﴿Until, when they came upon the valley of the ants, an ant said, "O ants, enter your dwellings lest Solomon and his soldiers crush you while they perceive not."﴾ [An-Naml: 18] (p-4663) ﴿So he smiled, amused at her speech, and said, "My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents, and to do righteousness of which You approve. And admit me by Your mercy into the ranks of Your righteous servants."﴾ [An-Naml: 19] ﴿And he inspected the birds and said, "Why do I not see the hoopoe? Or is he among the absent?"﴾ [An-Naml: 20] ﴿"I will surely punish him with a severe punishment or slaughter him, or he must bring me a clear authority."﴾ [An-Naml: 21] ﴿But he remained not long, and said, "I have encompassed [knowledge of] what you have not encompassed, and I have come to you from Saba' with certain news.﴾ [An-Naml: 22] ﴿"Indeed, I found a woman ruling them, and she has been given of all things, and she has a great throne.﴾ [An-Naml: 23] ﴿"I found her and her people prostrating to the sun instead of Allah, and Satan has made their deeds appealing to them and averted them from the way, so they are not guided."﴾ [An-Naml: 24] ﴿"[So] that they do not prostrate to Allah, who brings out what is hidden in the heavens and the earth and knows what you conceal and what you declare."﴾ [An-Naml: 25]

﴿And for Solomon were gathered his soldiers﴾, i.e., his armies were assembled for him, ﴿of the jinn and mankind and the birds, and they were marshaled in ranks﴾, i.e., he would hold back the first of them until the last of them caught up, so that they would join together. ﴿Until, when they came upon the valley of the ants, an ant said﴾ [An-Naml: 18], i.e., she saw them heading toward her valley. ﴿"O ants, enter your dwellings lest Solomon and his soldiers crush you while they perceive not"﴾ [An-Naml: 18], i.e., [they do not perceive] their location. ﴿So he smiled, amused at her speech﴾ [An-Naml: 19], i.e., out of wonder at her caution and her guidance to arranging the welfare of her own kind and theirs, and out of delight at the renown of his own state and that of his soldiers in the matter of piety and compassion among the kinds of created beings, which are the furthest of them from grasping such matters, and out of joy at what Allah the Exalted had singled him out with, namely, perceiving her whisper and understanding her intent. This is what Abu al-Su'ud said. ﴿"My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents"﴾ [An-Naml: 19], i.e., inspire me to thank You for it; ﴿"and to do righteousness of which You approve. And admit me by Your mercy into the ranks of Your righteous servants"﴾ [An-Naml: 19].

﴿And he inspected the birds and said, "Why do I not see the hoopoe? Or is he among the absent?"﴾ [An-Naml: 20]. ﴿"I will surely punish him with a severe punishment or slaughter him, or he must bring me a clear authority"﴾ [An-Naml: 21], i.e., a proof that makes his excuse clear. ﴿But he remained not long﴾ [An-Naml: 22], i.e., he stayed away for a period not long. ﴿And said, "I have encompassed [knowledge of] what you have not encompassed, and I have come to you from Saba'"﴾ [An-Naml: 22], which is a city, ﴿"with certain news"﴾ [An-Naml: 22]. ﴿"Indeed, I found a woman ruling them, and she has been given of all things, and she has a great throne"﴾ [An-Naml: 23], i.e., a seat upon which she sits, enormous and adorned with various kinds of jewels. ﴿"I found her and her people prostrating to the sun instead of Allah, and Satan has made their deeds appealing to them and averted them from the way, so they are not guided"﴾ [An-Naml: 24]. ﴿"[So] that they do not prostrate"﴾ [An-Naml: 25], i.e., *hallā yasjudū* (هَلّا يَسْجُدُوا, "why do they not prostrate"), as it was read. It is read with *tā'* (تُخْفُونَ, the second person) and with *yā'* (يَخْفى, the third person form). The exhortative clause (الجُمْلَةُ التَّحْضِيضِيَّةُ, *al-jumlah al-taḥḍīḍiyyah*) is either a new statement from the words of Allah the Exalted, or it is related as speech of the hoopoe. Al-Zamakhshari preferred the second view. He said: "Because bringing out what is hidden is a sign that it is from the speech of the hoopoe, due to his engineering skill and his knowledge of water beneath the earth. That [knowledge] comes by inspiration from He who brings out what is hidden in the heavens and the earth, may His power be exalted and His knowledge be subtle. And there is scarcely anything hidden, to one of penetrating insight who looks by the light of Allah, from the signs of every specialist in a craft or art or branch of knowledge, in his speech, his discourse and his bearing."

The exhortative clause (الجُمْلَةُ التَّحْضِيضِيَّةُ, *al-jumlah al-taḥḍīḍiyyah*) is either a new statement from the words of Allah the Exalted, or it is related as speech of the hoopoe. Al-Zamakhshari preferred the second view. He said: "Because bringing out what is hidden is a sign that it is from the speech of the hoopoe, due to his engineering skill and his knowledge of water beneath the earth. That [knowledge] comes by inspiration from He who brings out what is hidden in the heavens and the earth, may His power be exalted and His knowledge be subtle. And there is scarcely anything hidden, to one of penetrating insight who looks by the light of Allah, from the signs of every specialist in a craft or art or branch of knowledge, in his speech, his discourse and his bearing."

**On the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:**

[17–25] ﴿And for Solomon were gathered his soldiers of the jinn and mankind and the birds, and they were marshaled in ranks.﴾ ﴿Until, when they came upon the valley of the ants, an ant said, "O ants, enter your dwellings lest Solomon and his soldiers crush you while they perceive not."﴾ [An-Naml: 18] (p-4663) ﴿So he smiled, amused at her speech, and said, "My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents, and to do righteousness of which You approve. And admit me by Your mercy into the ranks of Your righteous servants."﴾ [An-Naml: 19] ﴿And he inspected the birds and said, "Why do I not see the hoopoe? (p-4665) The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[26] ﴿Allah! There is no god but He, the Lord of the Mighty Throne.﴾

﴿Allah! There is no god but He, the Lord of the Mighty Throne.﴾ That is: the One who encompasses the sun, the rest of the stars, and everything else. How small is its throne in comparison to His greatness! And how weak is its worshipped one, the sun, in the face of His power!

Caution (tanbih):

This prostration is one of the obligatory prostrations (ʿazaʾim al-sajadat). Al-Zamakhshari said: Because the places of prostration are either a command to prostrate, or praise for one who prostrates, or blame for one who abandons it. And one of the two readings is a command to prostrate, while the other is a rebuke against the one who leaves it.

The discussion on the interpretation of His, the Exalted's, statement:

[27–32] ﴿He said: "We will see whether you have told the truth or were among the liars. Take this letter of mine and deliver it to them; then withdraw from them and see what they return." (An-Naml: 28)﴾ ﴿She said: "O chiefs, indeed a noble letter has been delivered to me." (An-Naml: 29)﴾ ﴿Indeed it is from Solomon, and indeed it reads: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. (An-Naml: 30)﴾ ﴿Do not exalt yourselves over me, and come to me in submission. (An-Naml: 31)﴾ ﴿She said: "O chiefs, give me your opinion in my matter. I would not decide a matter until you witness it." (An-Naml: 32)﴾

﴿He said﴾, i.e., Sulayman: ﴿We will see whether you have told the truth or were among the liars. Take this letter of mine and deliver it to them; then withdraw from them and see what they return.﴾ ﴿She said: "O chiefs, indeed a noble letter has been delivered to me."﴾ i.e., its content and what is in it is good: ﴿Indeed it is from Solomon, and indeed it reads: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.﴾ ﴿Do not exalt yourselves over me, and come to me in submission.﴾ i.e., do not be arrogant toward me, and come to me submitting to my command. ﴿She said: "O chiefs, give me your opinion in my matter. I would not decide a matter until you witness it."﴾ i.e., I will not finalize a matter except in your presence and with your counsel, and I will not act independently in a judgment without seeking your views and referring to your consultation.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[33–35] ﴿They said: "We are possessed of great strength and great military might, but the command is yours, so consider what you will command."﴾ ﴿She said: "Indeed, when kings enter a town, they corrupt it and render its most honored people humble. And thus do they act."﴾ [An-Naml: 34] ﴿"And I am going to send them a gift, and will wait to see with what the envoys return."﴾ [An-Naml: 35]

﴿They said: "We are possessed of strength"﴾ meaning: in number and in equipment. ﴿And of great military might﴾ meaning: in valor and endurance in war. ﴿But the command is yours, so consider what you will command﴾ meaning: the matter of fighting or of reconciliation is entrusted to your opinion. So consider what is most lasting for your honor and your kingdom.

﴿She said﴾ [An-Naml: 34] meaning: indicating her preference for and inclination toward the policy of peace, in view of her own situation, her standing, and her weakness before her enemy. Fighting is only preferred when it is not overwhelmingly likely in one's estimation that the enemy will enter the enemy's town, and when submission is not clearly required. This is the meaning of her words: ﴿Indeed, when kings enter a town﴾ [An-Naml: 34], meaning: by force and coercion; ﴿they corrupt it﴾ [An-Naml: 34], meaning: they ruin it; ﴿and render its most honored people humble﴾ [An-Naml: 34], meaning: through compulsion, domination, killing, captivity, and plundering of wealth; ﴿and thus do they act﴾ [An-Naml: 34] is an affirmation of what she described of their condition and a confirmation that this is their constant custom. It has been said that it is a confirmation of her words by Him, Exalted is He.

﴿"And I am going to send them a gift, and will wait to see with what the envoys return"﴾ [An-Naml: 35], meaning: I will send to Sulayman and his council envoys with a gift that brings about affection and resembles submission, without diminishing our honor. Then I will wait to see with what matter the envoys return, so that I may act according to that.

(p-4667) The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[36–40] ﴿So when he (the messenger) came to Solomon, he said: "Will you provide me with wealth? What Allah has given me is better than what He has given you. Rather, you rejoice in your gift.﴾ ﴿Return to them, for we will surely bring them armies they cannot withstand, and we will surely expel them from there in humiliation, and they will be debased.﴾ [An-Naml: 37] ﴿He said: "O chiefs, which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?"﴾ [An-Naml: 38] ﴿A powerful one from the jinn said: "I will bring it to you before you rise from your place. Indeed, I am strong and trustworthy for it."﴾ [An-Naml: 39] ﴿One who had knowledge from the Scripture said: "I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you." And when he saw it settled in his presence, he said: "This is from the bounty of my Lord, to test me whether I will be grateful or ungrateful. And whoever is grateful, is grateful only for himself; and whoever is ungrateful, then indeed my Lord is Free of need and Generous."﴾ [An-Naml: 40]

﴿So when he came to Solomon﴾, i.e., the messengers from her: ﴿he said: "Will you provide me with wealth? What Allah has given me﴾, i.e., of kingship, wisdom and prophethood: ﴿is better than what He has given you﴾, i.e., I am not concerned with all that you have, let alone the gift: ﴿Rather, you rejoice in your gift﴾, i.e., when a similar gift is presented to you, or you are presented with a similar gift, you rejoice, out of pride in abundance or boasting.﴾ ﴿Return to them, for we will surely bring them armies they cannot withstand, and we will surely expel them from there in humiliation, and they will be debased﴾ [An-Naml: 37], i.e., abased. ﴿He said: "O chiefs, which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?"﴾ [An-Naml: 38] ﴿A powerful one from the jinn said: "I will bring it to you before you rise from your place﴾ (p-4668) ﴿and indeed I am strong and trustworthy for it."﴾ [An-Naml: 39] ﴿One who had knowledge from the Scripture said: "I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you." And when he saw it settled in his presence, he said: "This is from the bounty of my Lord, to test me whether I will be grateful or ungrateful."﴾ [An-Naml: 40], i.e., to try me: whether I will be grateful through obedience and acting by the Sharia, or ungrateful through disobedience and opposition.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever is grateful, is grateful only for himself; and whoever is ungrateful, then indeed my Lord is Free of need and Generous.﴾ [An-Naml: 40] is like His saying: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own self; and whoever does evil, it is against it﴾ [Fussilat: 46], and like His saying: ﴿And whoever does righteousness, they are preparing for themselves﴾ [Ar-Rum: 44].

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[41–42] ﴿He said, "Disguise her throne for her; we will see whether she is guided or is among those who are not guided."﴾ ﴿So when she came, it was said, "Is your throne like this?" She said, "It is as if it were it." And we were given knowledge before her, and we had been Muslims.﴾ [An-Naml: 42]

﴿He said, "Disguise her throne for her"﴾ means: make it unrecognizable, altered from its form and appearance, just as a man disguises himself from people. ﴿"We will see whether she is guided or is among those who are not guided"﴾ means: so that we may know it. ﴿So when she came, it was said, "Is your throne like this?" She said, "It is as if it were it"﴾ [An-Naml: 42]. Al-Mahayimi said: She did not say "It is it" (huwa huwa), out of fear of denial, together with some kind of alteration; nor "No" (la), out of fear of ignorance.

Al-Zamakhshari said: She did not say "It is it" nor "It is not it," and that is from the soundness of her intellect, in that she did not state with certainty what was uncertain. That is, she used "as if" (ka'anna), which indicates the predominance of assumption.

Al-Shihab said: This is an indication that "as if" (ka'anna) is not intended here as comparison but as doubt, which is well known for it.

The author of al-Intisaf has pointed out a distinction between "as if" (ka'anna) and "like this" (hakadha) in comparison. His words are: [p-4669] Her saying "It is as if it were it," and her departure from matching the answer to the question by saying "It is like this," is a fine point. Perhaps someone will say: both expressions are comparisons, since the comparison is in both of them, although in one it is attached to the demonstrative and in the other to the pronoun, and both of them (I mean the demonstrative and the pronoun) refer to the thing compared. In that case the two expressions are equal in meaning. Yet her saying "It is like this" is preferred for matching the question. So there must be a wisdom in choosing "It is as if it were it." We say: its wisdom, and God knows best, is that "It is as if it were it" is the expression of one whose resemblance has become so close that he doubts himself regarding the difference between the two matters, so that he nearly says "It is it," and that was Bilqis's state. As for "It is like this," it is the expression of one who is certain of the difference between the two matters, judging that resemblance alone exists between them. Therefore she turned to the phrase mentioned in the recitation, to match her state, and God knows best. End.

His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And we were given knowledge before her, and we had been Muslims﴾ [An-Naml: 42]. This is part of the speech of Sulayman, peace be upon him, thanking God for His favor upon them over her and their precedence to knowledge of God and of Islam. That is: we were given knowledge of God and of His power and of the truth of what came from Him, before her knowledge, which her saying "It is as if it were it" alluded to. The clause is coordinated with an implied element required by the context, which calls for elaboration in praising her for soundness of judgment in being guided to Islam. The sense is: she was right in her answer, having been granted Islam and knowing the power of God. "And we were given knowledge," etc. It has also been said that it is from the speech of Bilqis, joined to her saying "It is as if it were it," not from the speech of Sulayman, as if she thought he intended by that to test her intellect and to show her a miracle, so she said: "We were given knowledge," etc. That is: there is no need for testing, for I believed before. This indicates the perfection of her intellect.

Or the meaning is: we knew of your bringing the throne before the sight, or this state by the indications or the reports.

[43–44] ﴿And what she used to worship besides God had averted her [from faith]; indeed, she was of a disbelieving people.﴾ ﴿It was said to her, "Enter the palace." Solomon (peace be upon him) had built a wondrous palace of glass, and he wished to show her from it the greatness of his kingdom and authority, and the extent of what God had bestowed upon him. ﴿And when she saw it﴾ [An-Naml: 44], that is, its courtyard, ﴿she thought it was a [great] expanse of water﴾ [An-Naml: 44], that is, a great quantity of water. ﴿And bared her shins﴾ [An-Naml: 44], that is, in order to wade into it. ﴿[Solomon] said, "Indeed, it is a palace paved smooth"﴾ [An-Naml: 44], that is, made smooth. ﴿Of glass﴾ [An-Naml: 44], that is, of crystal. ﴿She said, "My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself"﴾ [An-Naml: 44], that is, by her former disbelief, her worship [of the sun], and her people's worship of the sun. ﴿And I submit with Solomon to God, Lord of the worlds﴾ [An-Naml: 44], that is, following him in his religion and in his worship of God alone, with no partner.

Remarks:

The first: Many exegetes have related here narratives whose chains are not authentic and whose reports are not sound. Such material is not permissible to transmit or narrate.

The Hafiz Ibn Kathir said, after citing what Ibn Abi Shaybah related from ʿAṭāʾ, approving of it, the following in substance: "I say: rather, it is very strange and extremely unusual. It is likely one of the errors of ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib upon Ibn ʿAbbās, and God knows best."

Then he said: "The closest explanation in contexts such as this is that they are taken from the People of the Book, from what is found in their scriptures, like the narrations of Kaʿb and Wahb, may God forgive them, in what they transmitted to this community of the reports of the Children of Israel, of the strange, the marvellous and the wondrous, some of which happened and some of which did not, some of which was altered, changed and abrogated."

God, glorified is He, has spared us from that by what is more authentic than it, more beneficial, clearer and more eloquent, and to God belong praise and grace.

The second: The Torah, in the fourth chapter of the Third Book of Kings, alludes to a detailed account of Solomon (peace be upon him) and the greatness of his kingdom and authority. Among what came in it is that Solomon ruled over all the realms from the river Euphrates to the land of Palestine and to the borders of Egypt, and that the kings of the regions used to bring him gifts, submitting to him all the days of his life, that is, they paid him tribute, even though he was confined to Palestine. God, exalted is He, gave him wisdom and a very keen understanding, and breadth of heart. His wisdom surpassed the wisdom of all the people of the East and the people of Egypt, and he uttered three thousand proverbs. He spoke about trees, from the cedar that is in Lebanon to the hyssop that grows out of the wall; he spoke about animals, birds, creeping things and fish. As for his palace and house (peace be upon him), its description came in the fifth chapter of the aforementioned book, and that he completed its building in thirteen years, and that he built Gezer, Beth-horon the Nether, Baalath and Tadmor in the wilderness. And in the tenth chapter of this same book there also comes the story of the Queen of Sheba and her coming from Yemen to Solomon to test his wisdom and the greatness of his kingdom, her astonishment at what she saw and verified, her belief in her Lord, exalted is He, then his granting her what she desired, and then her departure to her land.

We have mentioned more than once that the Noble Qur'an does not relate the reports of what has preceded in the manner of a historian, but rather recounts them concisely, so that it may be established that it confirms what lies before it and is a guardian over it, and to alert to the fact that the purpose of them is the place of lesson, wisdom, and the source of insight and discernment.

The third: Among what has been derived from the verses of this sublime story is that in His words, exalted is He, ﴿So he smiled, laughing, at her words﴾ [An-Naml: 19], there is no harm in smiling and laughing out of wonder or otherwise. In His words, exalted is He, ﴿And he inspected the birds﴾ [An-Naml: 20], there is a recommendation for a ruler to inspect the conditions of his subjects. Some have derived from it the inspecting of brothers [in faith], and so one of them recited:

Inspecting one's brothers is a commendable thing, and whoever initiates it has done well.
Solomon established for us a practice, and in what he established there was an example to follow.
He inspected the birds in his kingdom, and said: "Why do I not see the hoopoe?"

And in His words, exalted is He, ﴿I will surely punish him with a severe punishment﴾ [An-Naml: 21], and the verse that follows, there is evidence that punishment is according to the magnitude of the offence, not according to the size of the body. And [there is evidence] for the permissibility of disciplining animals and beasts by striking them when they fall short in walking, hasten, or the like. And in His words, exalted is He, ﴿He said, "I have encompassed [knowledge] of that which you have not encompassed"﴾ [An-Naml: 22], [there is evidence] that the junior may say to the senior, and the follower to the one followed: "I have knowledge that you do not have," when that is verified. And in His words, exalted is He, ﴿He said, "We will see whether you have told the truth or were among the liars"﴾ [An-Naml: 27], [there is evidence] for a ruler's acceptance of the excuse of his subjects, his averting punishment from them, and his testing their truthfulness in what they offered as an excuse. And in His words, exalted is He, ﴿Take this letter of mine and deliver it to them﴾ [An-Naml: 28], [there is evidence] for sending birds with letters. And in His words, exalted is He, ﴿It is from Solomon, and indeed it is: "In the name of God, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful."﴾ [An-Naml: 30]—no, the text here reads: ﴿Indeed, it is a noble letter﴾ [An-Naml: 29], [there is evidence] for the recommendation of sealing letters, according to the saying of al-Suddi: "Noble" means "sealed." And in His words, exalted is He, ﴿She said, "O chiefs, advise me in my matter"﴾ [An-Naml: 32], [there is evidence] for consultation and seeking opinions in important matters. And in His words, exalted is He, ﴿Do you provide me with wealth?﴾ [An-Naml: 36] and the verse that follows, [there is evidence] for the recommendation of refusing the gifts of polytheists. Thus [is stated] in al-Iklil, with additions.

Then God, exalted is He, informed about Thamud and what happened to them with their prophet Salih (peace be upon him), in His words, glorified is He:

The Hafiz Ibn Kathir said, after citing what Ibn Abi Shaybah related from ʿAṭāʾ, approving of it, the following in substance: "I say: rather, it is very strange and extremely unusual. It is likely one of the errors of ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib upon Ibn ʿAbbās, and God knows best."

Then he said: "The closest explanation in contexts such as this is that they are taken from the People of the Book, from what is found in their scriptures, like the narrations of Kaʿb and Wahb, may God forgive them, in what they transmitted to this community of the reports of the Children of Israel, of the strange, the marvellous and the wondrous, some of which happened and some of which did not, some of which was altered, changed and abrogated."

God, glorified is He, has spared us from that by what is more authentic than it, more beneficial, clearer and more eloquent, and to God belong praise and grace.

The second: The Torah, in the fourth chapter of the Third Book of Kings, alludes to a detailed account of Solomon (peace be upon him) and the greatness of his kingdom and authority. Among what came in it is that Solomon ruled over all the realms from the river Euphrates to the land of Palestine and to the borders of Egypt, and that the kings of the regions used to bring him gifts, submitting to him all the days of his life, that is, they paid him tribute, even though he was confined to Palestine. God, exalted is He, gave him wisdom and a very keen understanding, and breadth of heart. His wisdom surpassed the wisdom of all the people of the East and the people of Egypt, and he uttered three thousand proverbs. He spoke about trees, from the cedar that is in Lebanon to the hyssop that grows out of the wall; he spoke about animals, birds, creeping things and fish. As for his palace and house (peace be upon him), its description came in the fifth chapter of the aforementioned book, and that he completed its building in thirteen years, and that he built Gezer, Beth-horon the Nether, Baalath and Tadmor in the wilderness. And in the tenth chapter of this same book there also comes the story of the Queen of Sheba and her coming from Yemen to Solomon to test his wisdom and the greatness of his kingdom, her astonishment at what she saw and verified, her belief in her Lord, exalted is He, then his granting her what she desired, and then her departure to her land.

We have mentioned more than once that the Noble Qur'an does not relate the reports of what has preceded in the manner of a historian, but rather recounts them concisely, so that it may be established that it confirms what lies before it and is a guardian over it, and to alert to the fact that the purpose of them is the place of lesson, wisdom, and the source of insight and discernment.

The third: Among what has been derived from the verses of this sublime story is that in His words, exalted is He, ﴿So he smiled, laughing, at her words﴾ [An-Naml: 19], there is no harm in smiling and laughing out of wonder or otherwise. In His words, exalted is He, ﴿And he inspected the birds﴾ [An-Naml: 20], there is a recommendation for a ruler to inspect the conditions of his subjects. Some have derived from it the inspecting of brothers [in faith], and so one of them recited:

Inspecting one's brothers is a commendable thing, and whoever initiates it has done well.
Solomon established for us a practice, and in what he established there was an example to follow.
He inspected the birds in his kingdom, and said: "Why do I not see the hoopoe?"

And in His words, exalted is He, ﴿I will surely punish him with a severe punishment﴾ [An-Naml: 21], and the verse that follows, there is evidence that punishment is according to the magnitude of the offence, not according to the size of the body. And [there is evidence] for the permissibility of disciplining animals and beasts by striking them when they fall short in walking, hasten, or the like. And in His words, exalted is He, ﴿He said, "I have encompassed [knowledge] of that which you have not encompassed"﴾ [An-Naml: 22], [there is evidence] that the junior may say to the senior, and the follower to the one followed: "I have knowledge that you do not have," when that is verified. And in His words, exalted is He, ﴿He said, "We will see whether you have told the truth or were among the liars"﴾ [An-Naml: 27], [there is evidence] for a ruler's acceptance of the excuse of his subjects, his averting punishment from them, and his testing their truthfulness in what they offered as an excuse. And in His words, exalted is He, ﴿Take this letter of mine and deliver it to them﴾ [An-Naml: 28], [there is evidence] for sending birds with letters. And in His words, exalted is He, ﴿It is from Solomon, and indeed it is: "In the name of God, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful."﴾ [An-Naml: 30]—no, the text here reads: ﴿Indeed, it is a noble letter﴾ [An-Naml: 29], [there is evidence] for the recommendation of sealing letters, according to the saying of al-Suddi: "Noble" means "sealed." And in His words, exalted is He, ﴿She said, "O chiefs, advise me in my matter"﴾ [An-Naml: 32], [there is evidence] for consultation and seeking opinions in important matters. And in His words, exalted is He, ﴿Do you provide me with wealth?﴾ [An-Naml: 36] and the verse that follows, [there is evidence] for the recommendation of refusing the gifts of polytheists. Thus [is stated] in al-Iklil, with additions.

Then God, exalted is He, informed about Thamud and what happened to them with their prophet Salih (peace be upon him), in His words, glorified is He:

The discussion of the words of His Exalted Saying:

[45–47] ﴿And We had certainly sent to Thamud their brother Salih, [saying], "Worship Allah," but they became two factions contending.﴾ ﴿He said, "O my people, why do you seek to hasten evil before good? Why do you not ask forgiveness of Allah, that you may receive mercy?"﴾ [An-Naml: 46] ﴿They said, "We consider you and those with you to be a bad omen." He said, "Your omen is with Allah; rather, you are a people being tested."﴾ [An-Naml: 47]

﴿And We had certainly sent to Thamud their brother Salih, [saying], "Worship Allah," but they became two factions contending.﴾ (p-4673) That is: one faction believing and one faction disbelieving. "Yakhtasimun" (they contend) means a dispute in which the falsifier does not return to the truth after it has become clear to him. Like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿The eminent ones of his people who had been arrogant said to those who were oppressed—to those among them who had believed—"Do you know that Salih is sent from his Lord?" They said, "Indeed, we are believers in that with which he has been sent."﴾ [Al-A'raf: 75] ﴿Those who were arrogant said, "Indeed, we are, in that which you have believed, disbelievers."﴾ [Al-A'raf: 76] ﴿He said, "O my people, why do you seek to hasten evil before good?"﴾ [An-Naml: 46] That is: seeking the evil punishment before the good repentance. That is: why do you call for the punishment to be brought upon you, and not seek from Allah His mercy through faith? ﴿Why do you not ask forgiveness of Allah, that you may receive mercy?﴾ [An-Naml: 46] ﴿They said, "We consider you..."﴾ [An-Naml: 47] That is: we took an omen (tatayyarna), i.e., we considered it a bad omen (tashā'amna): ﴿you and those with you﴾ [An-Naml: 47], i.e., of the believers. And they, out of their wretchedness, whenever they were struck by some harm, would say: "This is from Salih and his companions." ﴿He said, "Your omen is with Allah"﴾ [An-Naml: 47], i.e., your path, from which comes your good and your evil, is from Allah. It is His decree and His apportioning: if He wills, He provides for you, and if He wills, He deprives you. Thus said al-Zamakhshari.

Al-Shihab said: Since the Arab traveler, when he set out, would pass by a bird that flew from his left—which is what is on his left side, called "sanih"—or from his right—which is what is on his right side, called "barih"—they would take the first as a good omen and the second as a bad omen. They attributed good and evil to the bird. Then this was borrowed for that which was the cause of both from the decree and apportioning of Allah, or from the deed of the servant, which is the cause of mercy and retribution. From this comes the expression "the bird of Allah," not "your bird": ﴿Rather, you are a people being tested﴾ [An-Naml: 47], i.e., you are afflicted by your misguidance and disbelief. You do not see good except what agrees with your desires, and you see no ill omen except in what opposes them. Then Exalted Allah informed about the tyrants of Thamud and their chieftains, who were the callers of their people to misguidance and disbelief, and to the denial of Salih, peace be upon him, and what became of them, with His saying, glorified is He:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 27, verses 48–52:

The interpretation of His statement, exalted is He:

[48–52] ﴿And there were in the city nine men who caused corruption in the land and did not reform.﴾ (p-4674) ﴿They said, "Swear to one another by Allah that we will surely attack him and his family by night; then we will say to his heir, 'We did not witness the destruction of his family, and indeed we are truthful.'"﴾ [An-Naml: 49] ﴿And they plotted a plot, and We plotted a plot, while they perceived not.﴾ [An-Naml: 50] ﴿So see how was the outcome of their plot: that We destroyed them and their people entirely.﴾ [An-Naml: 51] ﴿And those are their houses, ruined because they wronged. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who know.﴾ [An-Naml: 52]

﴿And there were in the city nine men who caused corruption in the land and did not reform.﴾ That is, their character and habit was corruption, as the present tense indicates, and its emphasis by His words "in the land" indicates the generality of their corruption. This phrase is a description of (rahṭ, "group of men") or of (tis'ah, "nine"). ﴿They said, "Swear to one another by Allah"﴾ [An-Naml: 49], that is, let each one of you swear in agreement with the others, by Allah, who is the greatest of those worshipped: ﴿we will surely attack him﴾ [An-Naml: 49], that is, we will kill him by night. It is also read with the letter tā' (lanubayyitannahu as "we will attack"), as addressing some of them to others. ﴿and his family﴾ [An-Naml: 49], that is, those who believed with him. ﴿then we will say to his heir﴾ [An-Naml: 49], that is, the one seeking his vengeance against us: ﴿"We did not witness the destruction of his family"﴾ [An-Naml: 49], that is, we were not present at the place of the family's destruction, let alone at its location, let alone at carrying it out, despite their being dispersed in many places. ﴿"And indeed we are truthful"﴾ [An-Naml: 49], that is, and we swear that we are truthful. Or: while the situation is that we are truthful regarding what we have mentioned. ﴿And they plotted a plot﴾ [An-Naml: 50], that is, with this stratagem. ﴿And We plotted a plot﴾ [An-Naml: 50], that is, by making them a cause of their own destruction. ﴿while they perceived not﴾ [An-Naml: 50].

﴿So see how was the outcome of their plot: that We destroyed them and their people entirely﴾ [An-Naml: 51].

﴿And those are their houses, ruined﴾ [An-Naml: 52], that is, empty and fallen down. They were not rebuilt after them, because they were utterly uprooted. ﴿because they wronged. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who know﴾ [An-Naml: 52], that is, that they were seized only for their wrongdoing. And indeed the end of wrongdoing is ruin and perdition.

Or: while the situation is that we are truthful regarding what we have mentioned. ﴿And they plotted a plot﴾ [An-Naml: 50], that is, with this stratagem. ﴿And We plotted a plot﴾ [An-Naml: 50], that is, by making them a cause of their own destruction. ﴿while they perceived not﴾ [An-Naml: 50].

﴿So see how was the outcome of their plot: that We destroyed them and their people entirely﴾ [An-Naml: 51].

﴿And those are their houses, ruined﴾ [An-Naml: 52], that is, empty and fallen down. They were not rebuilt after them, because they were utterly uprooted. ﴿because they wronged. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who know﴾ [An-Naml: 52], that is, that they were seized only for their wrongdoing. And indeed the end of wrongdoing is ruin and perdition.

Rather, you are a people who are ignorant."﴾ [An-Naml: 55] ﴿So the answer of his people was only that they said, "Expel the family of Lot from your town. Indeed, they are men who keep themselves pure."﴾ [An-Naml: 56] ﴿So We saved him and his family, except his wife; We had decreed her to be among those who remained behind.﴾ [An-Naml: 57] ﴿And We rained upon them a rain, and wretched was the rain of those warned.﴾ [An-Naml: 58] ﴿Say, "Praise be to Allah, and peace upon His servants whom He has chosen. Is Allah best, or what they associate?"﴾ [An-Naml: 59]

﴿And We saved those who believed﴾ means Salih (peace be upon him) and those with him. ﴿And they used to be God-fearing.﴾ ﴿And Lot, when he said to his people, "Do you commit immorality while you see?"﴾ [An-Naml: 54], meaning: its ugliness and its opposition to His judgment and wisdom. ﴿"Indeed, you approach men with desire instead of women"﴾ [An-Naml: 55], meaning: transgressing beyond the women who are the places of desire. ﴿"Rather, you are a people who are ignorant"﴾ [An-Naml: 55], meaning: you act like the ignorant, out of folly and blindness to the outcome. ﴿So the answer of his people was only that they said, "Expel the family of Lot from your town. Indeed, they are men who keep themselves pure"﴾ [An-Naml: 56], meaning: they distance themselves from our deeds and regard them as filth. They said this in mockery. ﴿So We saved him and his family, except his wife; We had decreed her to be among those who remained behind﴾ [An-Naml: 57], meaning: those who remained in the punishment. ﴿And We rained upon them a rain﴾ [An-Naml: 58], meaning: a terrible rain, unlike anything customary. ﴿And wretched was the rain of those warned﴾ [An-Naml: 58]. ﴿Say, "Praise be to Allah, and peace upon His servants whom He has chosen. Is Allah best, or what they associate?"﴾ [An-Naml: 59]

Al-Zamakhshari said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was commanded to recite these verses, which are clear in their proofs of His oneness, His power over everything, and His wisdom, and to begin by praising Him and sending peace upon His prophets and the chosen among His servants. In this is a fine teaching, an instruction in good manners, and an encouragement to seek blessing through the two remembrances, and to be strengthened by their place, so that what is conveyed to the listeners is accepted, they give ear to it, and it takes in their hearts the station that the speaker desires. The scholars, orators, and preachers have inherited this manner from generation to generation: they praise God, the Mighty and Majestic, and send blessings upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ before every beneficial branch of knowledge, before every admonition and reminder, and at the opening of every sermon. Those who write fluently followed them, and they placed it at the beginning of their letters concerning conquests, congratulations, and other events of importance. (p-4676) It was also said: it is connected to what comes before it, a command to praise God over the destruction of the disbelieving nations, and to send blessings upon the prophets, peace be upon them, and upon their followers who were saved.

Then he said: It is known that there is no good at all in what they associated, so that it could be weighed against the One who is the Creator and Owner of every good. Rather, this is a rebuke to them, a reproach, and a mockery of their condition, for they preferred the worship of idols over the worship of Allah. No sensible person prefers one thing over another except for a motive that calls him to prefer it, such as an increase in good or benefit. So they were told, while it is known that there is no good in what they preferred, and that they did not prefer it for an increase in good but out of desire and vanity, in order to alert them to their extreme error, the ignorance that ensnares them, their loss of discernment, and their rejection of reason. And so that they would know that preference must be for the greater good. A similar example is what He related about Pharaoh: ﴿"Am I not better than this one who is contemptible?"﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 52], though he knew that Moses did not have rivers like his that flowed beneath him.

Then He, glorified is He, enumerated the goods and benefits, which are the traces of His mercy and grace, as He enumerated them in another place. Then He said: ﴿"Is there any of your partners who does anything of that?"﴾ [Ar-Rum: 40]

A subtle point:

Ibn al-Qayyim said in (Tariq al-Hijratayn) concerning this verse: The word "peace" (al-salam) here may be taken as included within the scope of the speech, so that it is conjoined to the declarative clause, which is "Praise be to Allah," and the command to speak then covers both clauses together. On this reading, the pause falls on the last clause, and its position in i'rab is accusative, being reported speech after the verb of saying.

It is also possible that the clause is a separate, independent resumption, conjoined to the imperative clause. On this reading it has no place in i'rab.

On the first assessment, He commanded them to offer peace upon them.

The point is that on this view, Allah, exalted is He, has given peace to His chosen servants, of whom the messengers are the most excellent. End of quotation. And His saying, exalted is He:

**On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:**

[60–63] ﴿Is not He who created the heavens and the earth, and sent down for you water from the sky, with which We caused to grow gardens of delightful beauty, while you could never have caused their trees to grow? Is there a god along with Allah? Rather, they are a people who deviate.﴾ (p-4678) ﴿Is not He who made the earth a place of settlement, placed rivers through it, set firm mountains upon it, and placed a barrier between the two seas? Is there a god along with Allah? Rather, most of them do not know.﴾ [al-Naml: 61] ﴿Is not He who answers the distressed one when he calls upon Him, removes the evil, and makes you successors (khulafa') on the earth? Is there a god along with Allah? Little do you remember.﴾ [al-Naml: 62] ﴿Is not He who guides you in the darkness of the land and the sea, and who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy? Is there a god along with Allah? Exalted is Allah above what they associate with Him.﴾ [al-Naml: 63]

﴿Is not He who created the heavens and the earth﴾: This is a shift (idrab wa intiqal) from rebuke by allusion (tabkit ta'ridan) to explicit address (tasrih bihi khitaban) in a manner more manifest than it, for the sake of further emphasis. That is: "Rather, who created the heavens and the earth, and deposited in them benefits that cannot be counted?" ﴿And sent down for you water from the sky, with which We caused to grow gardens of delightful beauty﴾: that is, orchards of beauty and splendor that delight the beholders. ﴿While you could never have caused their trees to grow. Is there a god along with Allah?﴾: that is, is there another god existing along with Allah, who has mentioned some of His acts, which almost no one other than Him can perform, such that one would imagine that He could be made a partner to Him in worship? This is a rebuke to them by negating divinity from what they associate with Him, within a comprehensive negation in the demonstrative manner, after rebuking them by negating goodness from Him through the enumerated disjunction. Abu al-Su'ud said: ﴿Rather, they are a people who deviate﴾: that is, they deviate from the path of truth, or they ascribe to Him (exalted is He) something other than Him.

﴿Is not He who made the earth a place of settlement﴾ [al-Naml: 61]: that is, stable and not overturning those upon it, or a dwelling place for those upon it, who enjoy its benefits. ﴿Placed rivers through it, set firm mountains upon it, and placed a barrier between the two seas﴾ [al-Naml: 61]: that is, a barrier (barzakh) preventing intermixing. ﴿Is there a god along with Allah?﴾ [al-Naml: 61]: that is, in existence, or in originating these wonders. ﴿Rather, most of them do not know﴾ [al-Naml: 61]: that is, anything of things. Therefore they do not comprehend the falsity of the polytheism in which they are, despite its complete manifestness.

﴿Is not He who answers the distressed one when he calls upon Him﴾ [al-Naml: 62]: the distressed one (al-mudtarr) is the one whom illness, poverty, or some calamity of the times has compelled to seek refuge and to humble himself before Allah (exalted is He). It is an ism maf'ul (passive participle) from al-idtirar (ال اضطرار, "compulsion"), which is an ifti'al (reflexive verbal form) from al-darura (الضرورة, "necessity"), which is the state that compels one to seek refuge, that is, to resort to and lean upon Him.

Ibn Kathir said: He (exalted is He) draws attention to the fact that He is the One called upon in severe hardships, the One present at calamities, as He said: ﴿And when harm touches you at sea, those you call upon vanish except Him﴾ [al-Isra': 67]. And He said: ﴿Then when harm touches you, to Him you cry out for help﴾ [al-Nahl: 53]. Likewise He says here: ﴿Is not He who answers the distressed one when he calls upon Him﴾ [al-Naml: 62]: that is, who is it that the distressed one turns to only Him, and who is it that removes the harm of the afflicted other than Him?

Ibn al-Qayyim said in (al-Jawab al-Kafi): When supplication is accompanied by the presence of the heart and its complete concentration upon the desired object, and it coincides with brokenness before the Lord, humility before Him, supplication, and tenderness, and then one seeks a means (tawassul) to Him through His names, attributes, and oneness, this supplication is almost never rejected. This is especially so if it coincides with the supplications transmitted from the Prophet (ﷺ), for they are the most likely to be answered, or because they include the Greatest Name (al-ism al-a'zam, the name of Allah believed to be most effective in supplication). Then Ibn al-Qayyim cited them with their chains of transmission.

Then he said: We often find supplications by which people called, and they were answered, but that is because the supplication was accompanied by the supplicant's necessity and his turning to Allah; or because of a good deed he had previously done, for which Allah (glorified is He) made the answering of his call a thanks for his good deed; or because the supplication coincided with a time of answering, and the like, so his call was answered. Then the one who observes thinks that the secret lies in the wording of that supplication, and takes it in isolation from those matters that accompanied it from the supplicant. This is like when a man uses a beneficial medicine at the appropriate time and in the appropriate manner, and so he benefits from it; then another supposes that the use of this medicine by itself is sufficient to obtain the desired result, and he is mistaken. This is a point in which many people err. From this it may happen that his supplication under compulsion at a grave is answered; so the ignorant one thinks that the secret lies in the grave, and he does not know that the secret lies in the compulsion and the sincerity of seeking refuge in Allah. If this occurs in one of the houses of Allah, it is more excellent and more beloved to Allah. End of quotation.

﴿And removes the evil﴾ [al-Naml: 62]: that is, every evil that distresses, whether that in which one is compelled or otherwise. ﴿And makes you successors of the earth﴾ [al-Naml: 62]: that is, successors in it. This is their inheriting its inhabitants and their disposing of it, generation after generation (p-4680). Or he intended by khilafah (succession) kingship and dominion. Said by al-Zamakhshari. ﴿Is there a god along with Allah? Little do you remember﴾ [al-Naml: 62].

Exalted is Allah above what they associate with Him﴾ [al-Naml: 63].

The discourse on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[64–65] ﴿Is He not (best) who originates creation and then repeats it, and who provides for you from the heaven and the earth? Is there a god with Allah? Say: "Produce your proof, if you are truthful."﴾ ﴿Say: "None in the heavens and the earth knows the unseen except Allah, and they do not perceive when they will be resurrected."﴾ [an-Naml: 65]

﴿Is He not (best) who originates creation and then repeats it﴾, i.e., after death, by resurrection. If it is said: they deny the return, so how are they addressed with it as one who acknowledges it? It is answered: because of its manifestness and the clarity of its proofs, they were treated as if they acknowledged it, given their capacity to know it, so there remained no excuse for them in denial. There is no need to say that among them there were those who acknowledged it; the speech, with respect to him, is: ﴿and who provides for you from the heaven and the earth﴾, i.e., from what He sends down of its water and what He brings forth of its vegetation: ﴿Is there a god with Allah? Say: "Produce your proof, if you are truthful."﴾ This is a command to him, upon him be blessings and peace, to rebuke them further after a rebuke. That is: produce a proof, rational or transmitted, that indicates there is with Him, exalted is He, a god. Not a proof that other than Him, exalted is He, is able to do any of the deeds of His, exalted is He, that were mentioned, for they do not explicitly call upon Him (to such deeds). In the attribution of "the proof" to their pronoun there is a mockery of them, because of what it implies of the suggestion that they have a proof. And how could they have that? (This is) what Abu al-Su'ud said.

﴿Say: "None in the heavens and the earth knows the unseen except Allah"﴾ [an-Naml: 65], i.e., He alone is singular in that, as He said: ﴿And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them but He﴾ [al-An'am: 59], among countless verses (p-4681). For it includes Allah, exalted is He, and the people of knowledge among His creation. ﴿And they do not perceive when they will be resurrected﴾ [an-Naml: 65], i.e., when they will be raised up.

The discourse on the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:

[66] ﴿Rather, their knowledge has fallen short concerning the Hereafter. Rather, they are in doubt about it. Rather, they are blind to it.﴾

﴿Rather, their knowledge has fallen short concerning the Hereafter.﴾ Al-Samin (al-Samin al-Halabi) said: In this there are two views. The first: *fi* (in) retains its original meaning, and *adraka* (has fallen short/has overtaken), though past in form, is future in meaning, because it is certain to occur, as in His words: ﴿The command of Allah has come﴾ [al-Nahl: 1].

On this view, *fi* (in) is connected to *adraka*.

The second: *fi* (in) has the meaning of *ba'* (with/about). That is, *bi-al-akhirah* (concerning the Hereafter).

On this view, it is connected to their knowledge itself, as when you say: "My knowledge of Zayd is such-and-such." End of quotation.

The second view is that the verse is in the form of a question. That is: *bal hal adraka 'ilmuhum fiha*, meaning: "Has their knowledge reached and ended in it?" No. It has been read as *bal i'adraka* with two hamzas, *bal a'adraka* with an alif between them, *am adraka*, and *am tadaraka*.

Al-Razi said: This *am* is the one that carries the meaning of *bal* and the hamzah (of interrogation). So the meaning, in the form of a question, is a denial that their knowledge has reached it, and that they have not left the depths of ignorance regarding its truth, despite the proofs of its establishment that are recited to them.

Al-Suyuti and al-Mahayimi inclined toward reading the verse as a question. Others held that *bal* remains in its original sense of transitional change (*idrab intiqali*). They established this with an argument that is obscure and subtle, and it is refuted by the clear readings in the interrogative form that we have mentioned (p-4682), which are a reference point when the context is unclear, as is established in the rules of exegesis.

﴿Rather, they are in doubt about it﴾, that is, in misgiving, ﴿Rather, they are blind to it﴾, that is, in great confusion and ignorance, together with the establishment of what removes that doubt and uncovers its veil.

Al-Zamakhshari said: If you ask: what is the meaning of these three shifts? I say: they are nothing but a description of their conditions. He first described them as not perceiving at the time of resurrection; then as not knowing that the Hour is coming; then as floundering in doubt and misgiving, not removing it, though removal is possible. Do you not see that one who has not heard of the disagreement of the schools and their mutual condemnation of one another is in a better state than one who has heard of them and sits idle, with no effort to distinguish truth from falsehood? Then he described them with what is worse in condition: blindness, and being like a beast whose concern is fixed upon its belly and its private parts, with no thought of truth or falsehood and no reflection on the outcome. He made the Hereafter the origin and source of their blindness. For this reason he used *min* (from) rather than *'an* (about), because disbelief in the consequence and the recompense is what made them like cattle that neither ponder nor perceive. End of quotation.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 27, verses 67–70:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[67–70] ﴿And those who disbelieved said, "When we have become dust, and our fathers, will we indeed be brought out?" ﴾ ﴿Certainly we have been promised this, we and our fathers before. This is not but the fairy tales of the former peoples.﴾ [An-Naml: 68] ﴿Say, "Travel through the earth and observe how was the end of the criminals."﴾ [An-Naml: 69] ﴿And do not grieve over them, and do not be in distress because of what they plot.﴾ [An-Naml: 70]

﴿And those who disbelieved said﴾, i.e., concerning the promise of Allah and His signs, His knowledge, His power and His wisdom: ﴿When we have become dust, and our fathers, will we indeed be brought out?﴾, i.e., from the graves. ﴿Certainly we have been promised this, we and our fathers before. This is not but the fairy tales of the former peoples﴾ [An-Naml: 68], i.e., their tales and falsehoods which they inscribed in a deceptive expression. ﴿Say, "Travel through the earth"﴾ [An-Naml: 69], i.e., so that you may see the traces of those who said this statement before you. ﴿And observe how was the end of the criminals﴾ [An-Naml: 69] for their denial of it. The discussion of the words of God, Exalted is He:

[71–76] ﴿They say, "When will this promise be fulfilled, if you are truthful?"﴾ ﴿Say, "Perhaps some of what you are hastening for has drawn near to you."﴾ [An-Naml: 72] ﴿Indeed, your Lord is full of bounty toward the people, but most of them do not give thanks.﴾ [An-Naml: 73] ﴿And indeed, your Lord knows what their breasts conceal and what they declare.﴾ [An-Naml: 74] ﴿And there is not an unseen thing in the heaven and earth but that it is in a clear Record.﴾ [An-Naml: 75] ﴿Indeed, this Qur'an relates to the Children of Israel most of that over which they differ.﴾ [An-Naml: 76]

﴿They say, "When will this promise be fulfilled?"﴾ That is, the punishment. ﴿If you are truthful.﴾ ﴿Say, "Perhaps some of what you are hastening for has drawn near to you."﴾ [An-Naml: 72] That is, it has overtaken you or come close to you. ﴿Some of what you are hastening for.﴾ [An-Naml: 72] That is, of the punishment, and so there occurred to them the killing at Badr. But the punishment of the Hereafter is more bitter. Al-Zamakhshari said: "'Asa (perhaps), la'alla (perhaps) and sawfa (surely) in the promises and threats of kings indicate the certainty and seriousness of the matter, leaving no room for doubt after them. They only mean by this to display their dignity, and that they do not hasten vengeance, out of confidence in their power and dominance, and their certainty that their enemy will not escape them, and that a gesture toward their aims is sufficient on their part. Upon this the promise and threat of God proceed." End of quote. That is, because the true meaning of expectation is impossible with respect to Him, Exalted is He. Thus it is, according to this, a metaphorical figure of speech (isti'arah tamthiliyyah). Said by al-Shihab.

﴿Indeed, your Lord is full of bounty toward the people, but most of them do not give thanks.﴾ [An-Naml: 73] That is, He is truly bountiful and generous toward them, in delaying the punishment and not hastening it upon them. But most of them do not recognize the due of this blessing, so they do not give thanks for it; rather, out of their ignorance they hasten it.

﴿And indeed, your Lord knows what their breasts conceal and what they declare.﴾ [An-Naml: 74] That is, of enmity toward His Messenger and of setting snares against him. And He will punish them for that.

﴿And there is not an unseen thing in the heaven and earth but that it is in a clear Record.﴾ [An-Naml: 75] That is, there is no hidden thing in them, except that God has known it, encompassed it, and recorded it in the Clear Tablet, in which His decrees are inscribed. Or the intended meaning of "Book" is the just decree, by way of metaphor, likening it to the Book that gathers events, like a register.

﴿Indeed, this Qur'an relates to the Children of Israel most of that over which they differ.﴾ [An-Naml: 76] That is, it confirms what is before it and is a guardian over it. It relates the true narratives and decides between what they differed about with truthfulness. Thus, what is reliable of their reports is by it, and the final reference of what they differed about is to it.
