The Discussion on the Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[77–81] ﴿And indeed, it is a guidance and a mercy for the believers.﴾ ﴿Indeed, your Lord will judge between them by His judgment, and He is the Mighty, the Knowing.﴾ [An-Naml: 78] ﴿So rely upon Allah; indeed, you are upon the manifest truth.﴾ [An-Naml: 79] ﴿Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear, nor can you make the deaf hear the call when they turn away, retreating.﴾ [An-Naml: 80] ﴿Nor can you guide the blind away from their error. You can only make hear those who believe in Our verses, so they are Muslims.﴾ [An-Naml: 81]

﴿And indeed, it is a guidance and a mercy for the believers﴾, meaning: by what it contains of establishing proofs and removing doubts, which are understood by the believers who are fair-minded, who affirm the truth and submit to it. ﴿Indeed, your Lord will judge between them by His judgment﴾ [An-Naml: 78], meaning: between those who believe in the Qur'an and those who disbelieve in it, with His justice and wisdom. ﴿And He is the Mighty﴾ [An-Naml: 78], meaning: His judgment is not repelled, being dominant in His retribution against the falsifiers. ﴿The Knowing﴾ [An-Naml: 78], meaning: in making the decision between them and between the muhiqqun (those upon the truth). Then He, Exalted, commanded him to pay little heed to his enemies, and to proceed with his call and to await the promised true outcome, by His saying: ﴿So rely upon Allah; indeed, you are upon the manifest truth﴾ [An-Naml: 79], meaning: the clear, the one about which there is no doubt.

Al-Zamakhshari said: In it is an explanation that the possessor of the truth is worthy of trust in Allah's handiwork and His support, and that one like him is not forsaken. Then Exalted Allah pointed to the sufficiency of the benefit of his call for the believers, who are His allies and His party, and that all of them (the disbelievers) are not hoped to be guided, like the verse: ﴿And most of mankind, even if you strive eagerly, will not be believers﴾ [Yusuf: 103], as a consolation for what preoccupied him regarding their faith, by His, glorified is He, saying: ﴿Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear, nor can you make the deaf hear the call when they turn away, retreating﴾ [An-Naml: 80] ﴿Nor can you guide the blind away from their error. You can only make hear those who believe in Our verses, so they are Muslims﴾ [An-Naml: 81]. Al-Zamakhshari said: They were likened to the dead while they were living with sound senses, because when they hear what is recited to them of the verses of Allah, they are like funnels for speech, which their ears do not retain, and their hearing was as no hearing. Their state, due to the absence of any benefit from hearing, was like the state of the dead who have lost the faculty of hearing. Likewise is their likening to the deaf who are called and do not hear. (p-4686) The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[82] ﴿And when the word comes to pass against them, We will bring forth for them a creature from the earth, speaking to them that mankind did not believe in Our signs.﴾

﴿And when the word comes to pass against them, We will bring forth for them a creature from the earth, speaking to them that mankind did not believe in Our signs.﴾ Know that in this threat there are several aspects of interpretation:

The first: it is worldly (dunyawi), and by it is meant the victory of the Messenger, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, over them. The meaning is that those deaf to hearing the signs, blind to reflecting upon them, and denying them, will be given news of the reality of what they used to call to, namely the victory of the caller, who is the Messenger, and his followers, and the increase of their numbers until they prevail over their opponents and triumph over their enemy. This will come about when a great creature (dabbah) of the believers will crawl toward them, filling the plain and the hills, shaking their foundations, demolishing their structures, toppling their tents, and tearing down their banners. Then it will speak to them, at that time, with the tongue of the situation or of speech, telling them that they were only seized with punishment, and that severe torment has descended upon them because of their misguidance, their misleading of the servants, and their striving in the land for corruption. For faith is the pillar of righteousness and reform, and the leader of success and prosperity. Allah's word had already preceded to His messenger servants that they would surely be the victorious, and that His army would surely be the dominant. Allah has indeed fulfilled His promise and honored His army.

The second aspect: the dabbah is a living creature unlike what we know. Its emergence is specific to the time of the Resurrection. Some of them said: the meaning is that when the Resurrection occurs, Allah will raise a specific kind of creature of this earth, just as He raises other kinds of creatures. He will make it speak, and it will rebuke the human for his disbelief, just as He makes his limbs speak on that day as well. He said: so the intended meaning of His saying "a dabbah" is not a single individual but a kind, as in your saying: Allah sent upon them a worm (dudah) that destroyed their crops, meaning many worms of one specific kind.

Many reports and narrations have been transmitted concerning it, but al-Bukhari authenticated none of them, due to the confusion of their texts (p-4687) and the weakness of their narrators. The best of what has been transmitted is what Muslim narrated from Abdullah ibn Amr, traced to the Prophet: "The first of the signs to appear will be the rising of the sun from its west, and the emergence of the dabbah upon the people in the forenoon. Whichever of them occurs before the other, the other will follow it shortly."

It is known that matters of the Hereafter belong to the realm of the unseen, and nothing in them is taken except what is definitively established in transmission.

The third aspect: al-Raghib transmitted it in his Mufradat, saying: It has been said that by the dabbah is meant the wicked who are, in ignorance, in the position of beasts. Thus the dabbah is a collective noun, a name for everything that crawls, like kha'innah being the plural of kha'in. End of quotation.

Perhaps the verse is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Until when Gog and Magog are released, and they swarm from every mound﴾ [al-Anbiya: 96] ﴿And the true promise draws near, and behold, the eyes of those who disbelieved will stare: "Woe to us! We were heedless of this; nay, we were wrongdoers."﴾ [al-Anbiya: 97]. For Gog and Magog are like the dabbah, since by their crawling they cover the face of the earth, so it is a metaphor for multitude. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 27, verses 83–84:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[83–84] ﴿And on the Day We gather from every nation a company of those who denied Our signs, and they will be driven in ranks, until, when they have come, He will say, "Did you deny My signs while you did not encompass them in knowledge? Or what was it that you were doing?"﴾ [an-Naml: 84]

﴿And on the Day We gather from every nation a company of those who denied Our signs, and they will be driven in ranks﴾ means: their first is held back until their last joins them, so that they gather and are then hurled together into the Fire. This is an expression for the great number and the spread of its extremes, just as the armies of Sulayman (Solomon) were described with it. Likewise His saying, ﴿fawjan﴾ (a company), for a fawj is a large group. This is the view of az-Zamakhshari (al-Zamakhshari). ﴿Until, when they have come﴾ means: to the place of gathering. ﴿He will say﴾ means: in order to disgrace them on this witnessed Day. (p-4688) ﴿Did you deny My signs?﴾ meaning: those that speak of the meeting of this your Day. His saying ﴿while you did not encompass them in knowledge﴾ is a circumstantial clause (jumla haliyya) that serves to increase the enormity of the denial and the extent of its ugliness, and it reinforces the rebuke and reproach. That is: did you deny them at first glance, without looking into them with a examination that would lead to knowledge of their reality and that they are truly deserving of certain belief? This is explicit that what is meant by "signs" in the two places above is the Quranic verses, since they contain the proofs of soundness and the evidences of truthfulness, which they did not encompass in knowledge, while it was obligatory for them to reflect and ponder upon them, not the Hour itself and what is in it. This is the view of Abu as-Su'ud (Abu al-Su'ud). ﴿Or what was it that you were doing?﴾ meaning: with them. Or: what was your deed? Was it anything other than corruption and causing corruption, and barring the path of God from the servants? For this reason the word of punishment has become due against them, as He, exalted is He, said:

The Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on Surah 27, verses 85–89:

Discussion on the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[85–89] ﴿And the word will fall upon them for what they did wrong, so they will not speak.﴾ ﴿Have they not seen that We made the night for them to rest therein and the day giving sight? Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.﴾ ﴿And the day the Horn is blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will be struck with terror, except whom Allah wills. And all of them will come to Him humbled.﴾ ﴿And you see the mountains, thinking them rigid, while they pass as the clouds pass. [It is] the handiwork of Allah, who perfected everything. Indeed, He is Acquainted with what you do.﴾ ﴿Whoever comes with a good deed will have better than it, and they will be safe from the terror of that Day.﴾

﴿And the word will fall﴾, i.e., its meaning, which is the punishment they were promised: ﴿upon them for what they did wrong, so they will not speak.﴾ ﴿Have they not seen that We made the night for them to rest therein and the day giving sight﴾ — i.e., for them to see, by its light, the paths of movement in the affairs of livelihood: ﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.﴾ ﴿And the day the Horn is blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will be struck with terror, except whom Allah wills. And all of them will come to Him﴾ — i.e., they will be present at the place of standing before Him: ﴿humbled﴾ — i.e., abased. ﴿And you see the mountains﴾ is a conjunction with ﴿is blown﴾, included within the ruling of the reminder. ﴿Thinking them rigid﴾ — i.e., fixed in their places. ﴿While they pass as the clouds pass﴾ — i.e., through the dispersal and scattering of their parts, as in His saying: ﴿And the mountains will be like wool, fluffed up﴾ [al-Qari'ah: 5]. ﴿It is the handiwork of Allah, who perfected everything. Indeed, He is Acquainted with what you do﴾ — i.e., He will recompense them for it.

Note:

What we have mentioned in the interpretation of this verse is the view held by many. They said: the intended meaning of this verse is the moving of the mountains that will take place on the Day of Resurrection, when Allah Exalted destroys the worlds, as He said: ﴿And the mountains will be set in motion and become a mirage﴾ [an-Naba': 20], and as He said: ﴿And when the mountains are blown away﴾ [al-Mursalat: 10], and He said: ﴿And the mountains will be like wool, fluffed up﴾ [al-Qari'ah: 5].

Some of the astronomers said: it is not possible that the intended meaning of this verse is what they said, for several reasons:

First: His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿And you see the mountains, thinking them rigid﴾, does not suit the context of awe and warning if it is meant as what occurs on the Day of Resurrection. Likewise His saying: ﴿[It is] the handiwork of Allah, who perfected everything﴾ does not suit the context of destruction and annihilation. Moreover, placing this verse in the future, while it is clearly about the present, is a thing without any justification, and it contradicts its apparent meaning.

Second: The movement of the mountains to vanish on the Day of Resurrection occurs at the ruin of the world and the destruction of all creatures, and this is something no human sees, as He said: ﴿And the Horn will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will swoon, except whom Allah wills﴾ [az-Zumar: 68], i.e., of the angels. So what then is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And you see the mountains, thinking them rigid﴾?

Third: The movement of the mountains that occurs on the Day of Resurrection, if one sees it, one feels it, because as long as its position changes relative to the human being, he senses its motion. This contradicts His saying: ﴿thinking them rigid﴾, i.e., fixed. As for in this world, we do not feel their motion, because we move along with them and our position relative to them does not change. Then, the handiwork (sun') is the work of a human being after training in it, deliberation, and seeking to do it well. Note:

What we have mentioned in the interpretation of this verse is the view held by many. They said: the intended meaning of this verse is the moving of the mountains that will take place on the Day of Resurrection, when Allah Exalted destroys the worlds, as He said: ﴿And the mountains will be set in motion and become a mirage﴾ [an-Naba': 20], and as He said: ﴿And when the mountains are blown away﴾ [al-Mursalat: 10], and He said: ﴿And the mountains will be like wool, fluffed up﴾ [al-Qari'ah: 5].

This contradicts His saying: ﴿thinking them rigid﴾, i.e., fixed. As for in this world, we do not feel their motion, because we move along with them and our position relative to them does not change. This is something observed in the Qur'an from its beginning to its end. End of his words.

Al-Allamah al-Marjani said in the introduction to his book (Wafiyyat al-Aslaf wa Tahiyyat al-Akhlaf), in the discussion of the science of astronomy (hay'ah), the following, in substance:

The movement of the earth is indicated by His saying: ﴿And you see the mountains, thinking them rigid while they pass as the clouds pass﴾ [an-Naml: 88], etc. It is an address to the Messenger ﷺ, with the command primarily directed to him, while others share in this sight. The supposition that the mountains are rigid and fixed in their places, while they are in reality moving with the motion of the earth, and their continuous passing like the passing of clouds in the speed of travel and motion. He said: His saying: ﴿[It is] the handiwork of Allah﴾ [an-Naml: 88] is among the emphatic infinitives that confirm themselves, and it is the content of the preceding sentence, meaning that this passing is the handiwork of Allah.

Like His saying, Exalted is He: "The promise of Allah" and ﴿the dye of Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah: 138]. Then, the handiwork (sun') is the work of a human being after training in it, deliberation, and seeking to do it well. Not every action is called craftsmanship, nor every doer a craftsman, until he becomes skilled in it, trains in it, and is attributed to it. His saying: ﴿who perfected everything﴾ [an-Naml: 88] is like a proof of His perfection and an indication of the soundness of His creation and the arrangement of its passing in what is fitting. For the perfection of everything encompasses the perfection of its passing. So it is a repetition and reiteration of the intended meaning, like His saying: ﴿And whoever disbelieves, then indeed Allah is Free of need from the worlds﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 97]. He said: This verse includes aspects of emphasis and modes of exaggeration. Among them is His expression by "handiwork" (sun'), which is the beautiful, perfected act containing wisdom; its attribution to Him, Exalted is He, glorifies it and confirms the perfection of it and the goodness of His deeds. Then the description of Him, Glorified is He, with the perfection of everything, of which this passing is a part. Then its presentation in a nominal sentence, which indicates the permanence of this state and its continuance through the ages. Then the restriction by the circumstantial clause, to show that it never separates from them. For His saying: ﴿while they pass as the clouds pass﴾ [an-Naml: 88] is a circumstantial clause (hal) from the object, which is "the mountains," and it is governed by its verb, which is the seeing of them in that state.

This verse is therefore clear in its indication of the movement of the earth and the passing of the mountains with it in this created order. It is not possible to interpret it as referring to what happens in the next life, or at the establishment of the Hour and the corruption of the world and its departure from its customary order, nor that their being thought rigid is due to the non-visibility of the motion of great bodies when they are moving in one direction. For that does not suit the intended purpose of awe under that assumption. Moreover, that would be undoing and destruction, not handiwork and firm making. He said: It is strange that the expert scholars among the exegetes have not addressed this meaning, despite its being evident and despite the books of wisdom containing the statement of some of the earlier scholars. Furthermore, it is more fitting and more worthy to apply the possibilities of the Book of Allah to the weak Israelite narratives, with which they have filled their books. This is not outside the power of Allah, Exalted is He, nor far from His wisdom, nor does saying it contradict the Shari'ah or sound belief, provided one believes that everything came into being by the power of Allah, Exalted is He, His will, and His creation by choice, whatever it may be, and He is the Most High, the Great, and over all things is capable.

Know that this verse and what precedes it, from His saying: ﴿Have they not seen that We made the night﴾ [an-Naml: 86], etc., is a parenthetical insertion among the verses that present the conditions of the gathering and the terrors of the Resurrection, like the parenthetical injunction to a person concerning his parents within the story of Luqman. Such things are not rare in the Qur'an.

Its benefit here is alerting to the swiftness with which lifetimes come to an end and periods pass away, and warning of the sudden arrival of the hour of death and the nearness of the time of return. For the passing of times and the ending of periods happens only through the daily movement, passing at this speed which applies to human conditions. And this passing, although it is not seen or perceived, what arises from it of the change of states, through the succession of night and day and other things, is like the perceived and seen: ﴿So take warning, you who have sight﴾ [al-Hashr: 2]. Thus this is a miracle of the Prophet ﷺ, specific to him, since no other prophet was informed of it.

Therefore it is not possible to interpret the verse as referring to the moving of the mountains that occurs at the Hour and the fulfilment of the next creation, for that is not part of "handiwork" at all. Rather, it is the corruption of the states of beings, the disruption of the order of the world, and the destruction of the children of Adam. End of Marjani's words.

﴿Whoever comes with a good deed will have better than it, and they will be safe from the terror of that Day﴾ [an-Naml: 89] — i.e., that tremendous terror will not overtake them. It was read as (fazai' yawmi'idhin) with the genitive and kasra and fatha on the mim, and as fazain (tanwin) with fatha on the mim, on the basis that it is an adverbial complement of ("safe" — āminūn), or the elided item is an attribute of the terror. The tanwin in (yawma'idhin) is a substitute for an elided clause, i.e., "the day when they come with the good deed."

So He is the Creator of everything and its Owner. ﴿And I have been commanded to be among the Muslims﴾ [An-Naml: 91], that is, among those who submit their faces to Allah, not to anyone else.

Rather, He is Witness and Watcher, Majestic in His majesty and great in His bounty, and there is no god but Him.
